claims.text: The baseline alloy is equiatomic Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni.
The equiatomic Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni baseline has a single-phase FCC microstructure.
Reducing the constituent count to selected quaternary and ternary subsets increases local chemical short-range order.
Enhanced local chemical order alters dislocation core structures and their energy landscape.
Reducing constituent count produces a more uniform local chemical environment.
A more uniform local chemical environment reduces complexity at the dislocation core.
The modified dislocation-core energy landscape favors twin nucleation.
Reducing the constituent count can favor a deformation-induced FCC-to-HCP transformation.
In equiatomic CrCoNi, the FCC-to-HCP transformation is triggered by dislocation slip and interaction with internal boundaries.
Twinning or deformation-induced HCP formation can raise strength while retaining or improving ductility.
Selected quaternary and ternary subsets will simultaneously improve strength and ductility relative to the quinary baseline.
Quaternary and ternary alloys generally will exhibit higher twin densities than the quinary baseline.
Quaternary and ternary alloys generally will exhibit localized deformation-induced HCP formation relative to the quinary baseline.
The HCP transformation is specific to CrCoNi among the equiatomic ternary derivatives examined.
Removing costlier constituents may lower material cost and improve cost-performance balance.
Using identical thermomechanical processing and loading conditions can isolate the effect of local chemical ordering.
The proposed mechanism is limited to alloys that remain single-phase FCC under moderate temperatures and strain rates.
The mechanism may cease to apply after phase separation or at extreme temperatures or strain rates where other deformation mechanisms dominate.
The quantitative effect of local ordering on dislocation-core properties is uncertain.
The relative contributions of twinning and deformation-induced phase transformation are uncertain.

contradictions.description: The main hypothesis refers to selected subsets, but the predicted outcome generalizes enhanced twinning or HCP formation to quaternary and ternary alloys as classes. The cited evidence instead states that the HCP driving force was found only for CrCoNi and not for the other equiatomic ternary derivatives.
